speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and if you have any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and steroid use, is the ulcer surrounded by redness or warmth, and do you have any draining pus or a foul odor? Also, please confirm if you have any joint pain or abdominal symptoms recently.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein, Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work is normal, which is interesting given your history. Does the ulcer have a "punched-out" appearance with a pale or yellow base, and are you experiencing any eye pain, redness, or light sensitivity?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Antigen_Typhoid

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the negative typhoid result. Given your history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids and this ulcer's appearance, do you have any recent eye pain, redness, or light sensitivity, and can you confirm if the base of the ulcer looks yellow or necrotic?

REQUEST IMAGES: Close_up_of_skin_lesion

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum

The combination of a rapidly enlarging ulcer with a necrotic base and purplish, irregular borders in a patient with Crohn's disease, diabetes, and steroid use is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The reported "ant bite" was likely a coincidental event that precipitated the onset of the ulcer via the pathergy phenomenon.
